paper.title: Does Competence Make Citizens Tolerate Undemocratic Behavior?

claims.claim: The study included 2,481–3,159 respondents in each country.
claims.exhibit: Research Design and Data, p. 1148; Figure 1 note, p. 1151

claims.claim: There were 47,221–60,106 candidates in each country.

claims.exhibit: Research Design and Data; Figure 1 note

claims.claim: The pooled sample contained 267,795 candidate observations.
claims.exhibit: Research Design and Data; Figure 1 note

claims.claim: Undemocratic behavior effects ranged from −0.06 (South Korea) to −0.20 (United States).
claims.exhibit: Does Competence Suppress Sanctioning of Undemocratic Behavior?

claims.claim: The average effects of undemocratic behavior and competence were statistically significant at p < .001 in every country.
claims.exhibit: Does Competence Suppress Sanctioning of Undemocratic Behavior?

claims.claim: A one-unit increase in competence yields an effect of approximately 0.14–0.15 on support in each country.
claims.exhibit: Does Competence Suppress Sanctioning of Undemocratic Behavior?

claims.claim: In the Czech Republic, very incompetent candidates were sanctioned 0.13 points less than average-competence candidates (95% CI 0.05–0.21; p = .001).
claims.exhibit: Does Competence Suppress Sanctioning of Undemocratic Behavior?

claims.claim: The pooled survey experiments yielded more than 14,000 respondents.
The pooled survey experiments yielded more than 260,000 candidate observations.

findings.description: The supplied final dataset does not reproduce the article’s published sample counts. It contains 16,777 respondents and 335,540 candidate rows, against 14,058 and 267,795 in the Figure 1 note; country extrema also exceed the printed ranges.
findings.evidence: R import of package dataset.dta: 335,540 rows; 16,777 unique resp; country count output in logs/translated_analysis.log.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide the exact final analysis dataset used for the published results, or document the sample restriction that produces those counts.

findings.description: Data_prep.do cannot be rerun from this package: its raw country survey exports are absent, and the script references hard-coded U: drive paths. Stata is also unavailable.
findings.evidence: Package contains dataset.dta and scripts but no .tsv inputs; see logs/preparation-inputs.log. Data_prep.do imports ukmain.tsv first.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide the raw input files and a runnable environment or a fully specified translated preparation script.

findings.description: Analysis.do hard-codes the absent U: drive path to appendedfinal.dta. The analysis was instead translated to R and pointed to the supplied dataset.dta.
findings.evidence: The first command in Analysis.do uses U:\How to Save a Democracy\Data\appendedfinal.dta; translated run succeeded on the supplied dataset.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a relative path and document the exact dataset version.

limitations: The original Stata programs could not be executed because Stata is not installed.

The raw survey exports required by Data_prep.do are not included. Although the supplied final dataset allowed the primary published models to be translated and run, a command-by-command R translation of the entire 2,755-line preparation script was not produced; intermediate preparation outputs and any article claims dependent on them were not checked.
R translation of the main Figure 1 and Table A1 model commands only; models and figures not reported numerically in the article body were not rerun.
No robustness or scientific-validity assessment was performed.
